findings.latency: After each complete sample + PNG GET + decode the client waited 250 ms to begin the next sample. Accepted source input did not wake this loop. implementation.inputRefresh: The acknowledged inputSeq requests immediate sampling, with one sample in flight. implementation.sameN: The existing Debugger/global CSS pause boundary, isolated semantic reader, per-entry serial order and native visible-popup composition remain. implementation.concurrentStartup: Tracked creation operations retain owner/cancelled/pending. After shared wrapper startup, admission checks and entries.set are synchronous, preserving global/view/retained quotas while native.open calls run in parallel. closeView cancels pre-admission owners; shutdown drains tracked creations and actual native opening cleanup.
implementation.parallelAdmission: Tracked owner creations await shared startup; a synchronous quota/reservation segment admits entries before parallel native opens. Opening entries count toward view/global/retained limits. CloseView/shutdown cancel preadmission work, close retained creation.entry references and await tracked opening cleanup; late returns release contexts, grants and private profiles.
implementation.workerCollection: Layered batch pgrep on trusted parent PID lists then ps on only those requested child PID lists; requested PID, current trusted PPID and helper executable prefix must all match before ownership or traversal.

measurementBoundaries: Client display means the first successful drawImage commit to the visible .scene-canvas associated with its installed semantic frameSeq. It excludes OS compositor and physical display latency.

screencastRaw.boundary: Sole Page.screencastFrame PNG plus its attached metadata, top-level opaque CSP source. DOM scroll is observed separately; no PNG-afterward semantic repair, no retries, no tolerance.

limits: Page screencast metadata contains root viewport only, not nested scroll offsets or per-node transform/clip/sticky state.
Live DOM control values and layout geometry are not tied to a renderer semantic commit ID in the current protocol.
Applying a single root-scroll delta to all controls is incorrect for fixed, sticky, nested, and transformed containing blocks.
nativeScrollCapture.productionChanges: No failed scroll probe flags, virtual-time policy, external driver, direct-source navigation, or metadata correction were added to production.

capturedRootProof.statement: These captured root offsets match each attached PNG in the static stripe/row fixture. This does not establish full semantic-subtree consistency for arbitrary pages.

sourceFacts.fact: PageHandler reads scroll/scale metadata and pixels from the same delivered media::VideoFrame; CDP output omits engine frame_sequence and commit identity.

Capture populates VideoFrame from CompositorFrameMetadata then binds FrameCapture to asynchronous CopyOutputRequest. PendingCopyOutputRequest targets latest LocalSurfaceId. Full atomic source-frame association requires an engine guarantee beyond the twelve observed root pairs.

Programmatic smooth scroll creates a CC SCROLL_OFFSET animation unless ShouldScrollOnMainThread; fallback uses the existing main-thread animation curve. Current public setting exposes no hard per-runtime main-scroll/freeze guarantee.
Direct compositing reasons override the weak non-composited scroll preference; preference does not force all nested/transform scrollers onto one source clock.

missingTypedData: A renderer semantic snapshot identity associated with the active compositor commit; labels, values, DOM text and reading order can change independently of root scrolling.

For each semantic fragment/node: stable native owner identity, local geometry, committed transform/scroll/clip associations and the native frame-resolved viewport quad plus clipping; one bounding rectangle and root delta do not cover transforms or fragments.
Nested scroll offsets and their actual frame-resolved scroll/transform tree; rootScrollOffset remains unchanged during nested compositor scroll.
Fixed containing-block and sticky constraints resolved at that actual compositor frame, including transformed ancestors, clipping and viewport/page scale.
For wrapper/OOPIF: frame-owner embedding transform/clip and per-source renderer commit identities, kept within current opaque sandbox and asset/permission boundaries.

minimalExtensionAlternatives.boundary: Freeze compositor animation/frame clock at a selected frame without canceling source smooth scroll, apply/drain all impl-to-main scroll deltas, acknowledge renderer state, run the isolated semantic reader and copy that same submitted frame, then resume in finally. Public CEF BeginFrame lacks timestamp/freeze/drain acknowledgment.

renderer scroll-state/commit acknowledgment across widget boundaries

minimalExtensionAlternatives.boundary: At renderer commit, retain semantic values and fragment/property bindings; at active compositor frame, resolve native transform/scroll/clip geometry and return it with pixel capture and engine commit/frame identifiers. rAF/CSS FPS counts source requestAnimationFrame callbacks and distinct computed CSS positions. Native paint FPS counts actual CEF OnPaint events; it does not inspect every compositor pixel.
CPU is own CEF process tree cumulative ps CPU-time delta; RSS is instantaneous. Existing user CEF pages remain active. Phase snapshots and protocol calls add measurement overhead.
Input-to-pair means Node-side native input dispatch to the returned consistent PNG/metadata pair, excluding frontend HTTP/decode/compositor display. Frontend click latency is measured separately.

rendererTail.conclusion: The fixed original object reproduces an approximately two-second interval between complete response and document interactive in both worker implementations. Preview read/end/finish complete in about one millisecond in that original long-tail row; DNS/connect timings are zero. Network/DNS/host mapping is not supported as the cause. These timestamps localize a renderer document-lifecycle interval; no native renderer trace was collected to distinguish parsing CPU, task deferral or an engine lifecycle dependency.
